Short answers and suggested customer-facing language below. I also attached a draft DSR handling playbook and the latest DPA + SCC bundle to this thread.

Controller/Processor (single-paragraph):
"Redwood Inference acts as a data processor for customers using the hosted API and for Redwood-managed Dedicated deployments. The customer (Acme Corp) is the data controller for data submitted to and generated by the integration; Acme is responsible for verifying identity, lawful basis, and responding to data subject requests. For on-prem or customer-managed private deployments where Redwood is not operating the environment, Redwood is not processing customer data on behalf of the customer and therefore is not a processor. Where Redwood provides managed services in a private deployment, Redwood remains a processor as specified in our DPA."

Deletion propagation (hosted API) — summary matrix:
- Runtime KV cache (inference cache): logical delete applied within 1 hour; hard purge as part of regular shard compaction within 7 days.
- Short-lived request logs (CPU/GPU traces): logical redaction within 24 hours; persisted traces removed on 30 day rotation; backups may contain copies for up to 90 days (see backup retention).
- Analytics/metrics (aggregated usage): aggregated/anonymous counts updated within 24 hours; no PII stored in aggregated metrics.
- Embedding stores (hosted optional feature): immediate deletion from hot storage within 24 hours; cold backups purged up to 90 days depending on snapshot window.
- Backups / disaster recovery snapshots: snapshots retained per contract (default 90 days), deletions are scheduled on snapshot expiry; emergency restores will follow the same deletion propagation rules after restore.

Notes:
- We consider most runtime caches and embedding stores as "logical deletes" with subsequent hard purge windows to ensure safety across distributed storage and snapshot consistency.
- Where customers require accelerated hard-delete SLAs, we can offer a dedicated contract amendment (Dedicated/Private runs) to shorten purge windows.

Evidence bundle (recommended):
- Redwood DPA (latest signed copy) — ok to share.
- SCC addendum PDF — ok to share.
- SOC 2 Type II: we share an executive summary; full report is available under NDA only.
- SIG status: provide completed CAIQ/SIG summary (redacted) and a link to our security portal.
- DSR handling playbook — share the high-level (non-opsec) version; internal runbook remains internal.

I'll attach: redwood-dpa-v3.pdf, scc-addendum-2026.pdf, dsr-handling-playbook-v2.md, deletion-propagation-diagram.png. Marissa — any immediate concerns?

Thanks,
Kar
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi Sara — following up with the materials and a plain-language reply you can use to respond to the user. Attached: redwood-dpa-v3.pdf, scc-addendum-2026.pdf, dsr-handling-playbook-v2.md, deletion-propagation-diagram.png. See language below for your customer-facing response.

Customer-facing language (suggestion):
"Thanks for contacting Acme about your data. To be transparent: Acme is the data controller for the information you submitted to Acme's services. Acme uses Redwood Inference to process certain requests; Redwood acts as a data processor for the hosted API and is bound by Acme's instructions and our Data Processing Agreement. In practical terms, when Acme requests deletion, Redwood will apply a logical deletion to runtime caches within 1 hour and proceed with hard purges according to our snapshot and backup retention schedule (hard purge within 7–90 days depending on the storage tier). Acme will coordinate any immediate follow-ups with Redwood if accelerated deletion is required."

Deletion timeline (high level):
- Runtime inference cache: logical delete within 1 hour; hard purge within 7 days.
- Short-term logs/traces: logical redaction within 24 hours; physical removal on 30-day snapshot rotation.
- Embeddings/hot storage: remove from hot storage within 24 hours; backups purged within 90 days depending on snapshot windows.

Attachments included in this message: redwood-dpa-v3.pdf (DPA), scc-addendum-2026.pdf (SCC addendum), dsr-handling-playbook-v2.md (customer-facing runbook), deletion-propagation-diagram.png (illustration).

If you want us to accept a verified DSR forwarded from Acme and perform the deletion action on our side, we are happy to do that provided Acme confirms the request and provides the account identifier or request id. Otherwise, Acme as controller should respond to the user and notify us if they want Redwood to execute the deletion.

Let me know if you need the SOC 2 executive summary (we can share under the mutual NDA) or an expedited purge amendment — happy to set up a short call with Kar and our Ops team (Vivek) if needed.
